name: gizza-ai/confusion-matrix
summary: Build a confusion matrix and classification metrics

tool.description: Build a confusion matrix and classification report from true vs predicted labels. Accepts two label columns, an actual/predicted table with optional counts, or a square matrix grid. Reports per-class precision, recall, F-score, specificity, support, macro/weighted/micro averages, accuracy, balanced accuracy, Cohen's kappa, Matthews correlation, and an expanded binary summary with Wilson confidence intervals when a positive class is available. Supports label ordering, row/column/all normalization, F-beta weighting, decimal precision, percentages, and markdown/text/CSV/JSON output.

actual.description: True labels, one per row; or paste a complete actual,predicted[,count] table or a square confusion-matrix count grid when predicted is empty.

beta.description: F-beta weight for the report. 1 gives F1; values above 1 weight recall more heavily.

decimals.description: Decimal places for rates and scores.

format.description: Output format for the matrix and metrics.

header.description: Whether the first row is a header. Auto recognizes common actual/predicted header names.

input_format.description: Input shape: auto (default), two separate label lists, an actual/predicted table, or a square confusion-matrix grid of counts.

labels.description: Optional class order, separated by commas, newlines, tabs, semicolons, pipes, or spaces. Unseen labels are included with zero support.

normalize.description: Normalize matrix cells by row, by prediction column, or by all observations; none returns raw counts.

percent.description: Show proportions as percentages in text, markdown, and CSV output.

positive_label.description: Positive class for the binary summary. When blank and exactly two classes exist, the tool chooses a common positive label or the second class.

predicted.description: Predicted labels, one per row. Leave empty when actual contains a paired table or matrix grid.

separator.description: Separator for labels or table columns. Auto accepts newlines, comma, tab, semicolon, pipe, and falls back to whitespace.
